name: JARVIS ComfyUI — On-Device Image Generation
summary: Local text-to-image generation via a running ComfyUI instance (Stable Diffusion). Queues a generation workflow, polls until completion, and returns the output as a base64-encoded PNG — entirely on-device, no cloud API, no data leaves the machine. GPU-dependent: requires a model checkpoint loaded in ComfyUI.

transports.description: JARVIS ComfyUI MCP Server (stdio). Stdlib only — bridges to a local ComfyUI HTTP API.

tools.name: generate_image
tools.description: Generate an image from a text prompt using a locally running ComfyUI instance. Queues a Stable Diffusion workflow, waits for completion and returns the image as a base64-encoded PNG. Runs entirely on-device — no cloud API, no data leaves the machine.

tools.name: list_models
tools.description: List the model files available in the running ComfyUI instance, grouped by type (checkpoints, loras, vae, etc.). Use to discover valid model filenames for generate_image.

tools.name: get_queue
tools.description: Show the current ComfyUI queue: pending and running prompts.

tools.name: interrupt
tools.description: Stop the currently running ComfyUI generation.

tools.name: get_history
tools.description: Return the most recent generation history from ComfyUI: prompt IDs and output filenames.

configurableProperties.label: ComfyUI Server URL
configurableProperties.description: Base URL of the running ComfyUI instance. Default http://127.0.0.1:8188. Change only if you started ComfyUI on a different host or port.

checks: license: same as this registry (GPL-3.0), first-party server
build: none — Python standard library only (urllib, json, base64); setup.sh installs nothing
no third-party Python dependencies, no subprocess calls
network: only the COMFYUI_URL host (127.0.0.1:8188 by default); no other outbound calls
no filesystem writes — images read into memory and returned as base64; ComfyUI writes its own output_dir
trust.notes: First-party server. Thin HTTP bridge to a locally running ComfyUI instance. Stdlib only. The server itself is low-risk; the GPU and model resources it drives are the user's own hardware. Generated images are returned as base64 content blocks and not cached by this server.
trust.securityNotes: All requests go to COMFYUI_URL — a local endpoint by default. No credentials are required or accepted. Generated images are read into memory, base64-encoded and returned in the MCP response; they are never written to disk by this server (ComfyUI itself writes output_dir). The interrupt tool can abort an in-progress generation, which is useful if the agent queues something unintended. generate_image blocks for up to 10 minutes waiting for completion; the suggestedRemindAfter hint is 60 seconds so the orchestrator can report progress. The COMFYUI_URL config allows targeting a non-local ComfyUI server — if changed to a remote URL, generation prompts and images traverse the network unencrypted unless ComfyUI is behind TLS.
